title: claimspec v1 — calibration
description: The observed rate of a bucket's outcome — for testguard, the share of real escaped bugs of a fault class that the suite failed to catch, so a high p is bad — with a confidence interval and the sample size behind it. A label without n is a vibe; this is the format that stops it being one. p and ci are recomputable from n, positives, method and confidence, and the validator recomputes them. Everything beyond the primary buckets is optional and additive, as `method` is on claims and evidence: a document that omits `measures` or `source.caveat` stays valid and is UNATTRIBUTED — a consumer may read it and audit it, merge nothing into it, and quote no number from it.

method.description: Interval method. `wilson` is the only method defined in v1; under it the point estimate is the observed proportion positives / n, and a smoothed or shrunk estimate is a different method.

measures.description: What `p` is the probability of — the one field that lets two calibrations be told apart. Registry in GATE-SEMANTICS.md: `escape-missed` (testguard: a real escaped bug of this class was not caught; high is bad) and `finding-real` (websec-validator: a reported finding of this class is a real vulnerability; high is good). Two documents merge only when this, `bucketBy` and `confidence` agree. Absent = unattributed: nothing may be quoted from the document.

bucketBy.description: The field findings are bucketed on, e.g. `faultClass` or `severity`. A compound key joins fields with `|` (`attackClass|confidence`), and every bucket key then has the same number of parts.

minN.description: The producer's floor. A cell with fewer samples is not quoted on its own; the consumer backs off a tier, then to `fallback`, then to nothing. A consumer may raise this — a gate that blocks a merge wants more certainty than a report — and may never lower it: lowering it resurrects a cell the producer suppressed. Absent = the producer sets no floor and the consumer applies its own.

source.description: Where the ground-truth labels came from. `kind` is the mechanism (`tool-oracle`: a tool confirming its own findings, as websec-validator's dynamic probes do). `corpus` names external ground-truth sources — a bug-replay's ground truth is the repository's own history, already named by `ref`, so it is usually absent there. `caveat` is the one sentence a consumer must show beside any quoted number; `limitation` is the longer story; `evidenceStatus` says whether the labels were reviewed. `detail` is the tool's own provenance, deliberately unconstrained, on the `methodDetail` pattern: what the first consumers put there is the evidence for what should become specified.

backoff.description: Ordered coarser tiers consulted when a primary cell is below `minN`: websec-validator's `attackClass|confidence` backs off to `confidence`. Each tier is held to the same arithmetic as the primary. Absent = no backoff.

fallback.description: What remains when no tier has a cell above `minN`: a labelled guess, not a measurement, and the shape says so — it has a `basis` and no `n`, and anything quoted from it carries n = 0, ci = [0, 1] and the basis. It lives in the document so that "what did it assume when it had no data?" has one auditable answer instead of one per consumer.

p.description: positives / n at the document's precision, or null when n = 0: a cell with no trials has no proportion, and 0 would be a fabricated one.

breakdown.description: How n splits by outcome, when the producer can say (testguard: caught / blind / nocover). Values sum to n. Lets a consumer recover a narrower rate — misses among covered code, say — without the producer publishing a second, misleading headline.
